title: Stitch runtime routing state for version pinning, staged rollouts, and region/tier fallthroughs
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Runtime decisions that resolve a request's route (region selection, tier routing, and model variant fallback) are currently evaluated in separate subsystems. During staged rollouts and when requests carry pins/affinities, outcomes can diverge between the controller's plan and the serving runtime's actual route. This causes: 1) sticky sessions to receive unexpectedly different model variants mid-rollout, 2) telemetry gaps where the Console's rollout chart disagrees with observed token latencies, and 3) flaky canary metrics when clients are routed across tiers/regions for the same version affinity.

Goal: Implement a deterministic stitching layer in the serving runtime that reconciles pinning, staged-version policies (canary/A-B), region preferences, and tier fallthrough rules into a single, auditable routing decision for each request. The layer must be lightweight, compatible with existing smart routing policies, and observable (emit decision reasons and keys).

Scope: Runtime-only changes for the route resolver and decision telemetry. UI/controller orchestration changes will be handled in a follow-up ticket. This work must not change existing policy syntax; it implements a precedence and state-stitching engine inside the runtime so behavior matches controller expectations during rollouts.
tasks: Design policy precedence DAG and canonical evaluation order
Define deterministic stitch keys for request context (user-pin, session-id, geo, tier, version-hint)
Implement Affinity Reconciler component in the route resolver
Add decision_reason and stitch_key to runtime traces and Console ingestion payloads
Create unit + integration tests covering pin+canary+region permutations
Perf test with high QPS traffic profile (verify no regressive latency)
Document runtime guarantees and telemetry fields for Console teams
acceptance_criteria: Requests with existing version pins remain sticky to the pinned variant unless the policy explicitly expires or the variant is removed
During a staged rollout, requests matching the canary cohort see the canary variant deterministically and non-cohort requests follow fallback logic consistently
Region and tier fallthroughs are applied as a single canonical decision; Console charts match runtime-emitted decision_reason over a 1-hour window
Added trace fields do not exceed 2% of request payload size and pass privacy review
Unit and integration tests for 12 permutations (pin/no-pin x canary/cohort x regional/tier failover) are green
No significant tail-latency regressions in P95/P99 under the standard perf job compared to baseline
design_notes: Evaluation model: build a small precedence DAG where nodes are (explicit pin, version-affinity, regional-preference, tier-preference, degrade-policy, fallback-variant-set). The graph is evaluated left-to-right with early-exit only when a node yields a concrete variant or a permanent exclusion
Stitch key: 64-bit opaque token derived from (customer-id || route-id || session-id || device-fingerprint) hashed with a stable seed. Stitch key is included in traces for correlation and TTL checks

Affinity Reconciler: maintains short-lived sticky maps only when a pin is explicit. For probabilistic canary cohorts we do not persist state server-side; cohort membership is computed from the stitch key and rollout percentage to remain stateless across runtime nodes

Fallback semantics: fallback sets are ordered and annotated with degrade thresholds. When a preferred variant is overloaded or unavailable, the reconciler advances to the next candidate but records the degrade_step in decision_reason
Observability: emit 'decision_reason' (enum) and 'stitch_key', plus 'applied_policy_snapshot' (compressed tag list) to traces. Console will parse these to reconcile rollout charts
Safety: introduce a circuit-breaker that rejects sticky-mutations if KV store latency exceeds threshold to avoid blowing SLOs
tradeoffs: Stateful vs stateless: we avoid global persistent sticky maps to keep the runtime horizontally scalable. This means explicit pins are honored by a local ephemeral store; cross-node stickiness relies on stable client-provided stitch keys (session-id).
Trace payload vs observability: adding decision metadata increases payload size slightly; we compress and cap fields to meet privacy/storage budgets
Deterministic cohort computation trades flexibility (no server-side cohort targeting by attributes) for simplicity and consistency across nodes
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Existing clients without session ids may receive inconsistent variants across requests. Mitigation: if session-id is missing, log a warning and fall back to region-first deterministic hashing based on client IP
Risk: Additional decision logic adds CPU cost. Mitigation: micro-benchmark code paths and inline hot paths; feature-flag rollout to throttle CPU impact
Risk: Telemetry mismatch with Controller during initial rollout. Mitigation: run dual-emission mode where runtime also emits expected-controller-decision for first 48 hours for cross-checking
qa_plan: Unit tests for precedence rules and edge cases (variant deleted mid-stitch)
Integration tests spanning multiple runtime nodes to verify stateless cohort behavior
Canary deployment to 5% of teams with verbose logs enabled, compare Console reconciliation reports
Load test at expected peak QPS and 2x to ensure no P99 regressions
deployment_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: off -> verbose-emission-only -> reconcile-mode -> default-on
Start in verbose-emission-only mode where runtime emits decision_reason but continues to follow legacy resolver (2 days)
Enable reconcile-mode for a small set of internal customers and monitor discrepancies (3 days)
Full flip to default-on after 7 days of low discrepancy metrics or manual sign-off
Post-deploy runbook: rollback flag and KILL switch available if discrepancy rate > 1% or P99 degrades > 10%

Recommend a short customer-facing doc describing deterministic cohort semantics and recommended client-side session-id usage for stickiness
